findings.file: tools/check-browser-install.py:_builtin_call_problem (the `eval` branch, ~line 1253 of the working tree), and the docstring sentence 'a builtin on BUILTINS called in the one shape its row allows' / BUILTINS row for eval 'the reader holds it to that stub's output'
findings.issue: contradicts task clause 1 ('NOTHING the action's shell starts may be anything but a stub or an allow-listed tool'; hold it as a positive rule): the `eval` shape check accepts a double-quoted word that starts with `"$(`, ends with `)"`, has exactly one substitution and that substitution is `apt-config`, but it never checks the characters between. So `v='; ../../../../../../../../bin/echo ESCAPED #'` followed by `eval "$(apt-config shell s D/d)$v)"` has script_problems() == [] (I ran script_problems on that text with the module imported, no writes: it returned []), and the same text under plain bash started the real /bin/echo through a relative path (output ESCAPED). The reader reads the single-quoted assignment as a literal, the prelude disables no program started by a slash path and sd7 sees no absolute path, so both halves are passed and the docstring's claim that eval is held to the stub's output is false. bp10 only has `eval "$x"`, which is why the row stays green.
findings.resolution: Hold eval to the exact word, not to its first and last characters: accept only a text that matches a fixed shape such as `^"\$\(apt-config [A-Za-z:/ ]+\)"$` (nothing between the substitution and the quotes, no `$`, backslash or quote inside), or have _word record that a dq word is one substitution and nothing else. Add bp10 rows for `eval "$(apt-config shell s D/d)$v)"` and `eval "$(apt-config x) ; y"`, and a bx row that appends the variable-assignment plus eval pair with the file outside, refused by the reader.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause 1: the printf rule is `args[0]["quoted"] == "sq"`, 'so it is never `-v`' (BUILTINS row, docstring). Quote removal happens before the builtin sees its arguments, so `printf '-v' 'a[$(../../../../../../../../usr/bin/touch x)]' y` has script_problems() == [] (ran it, no writes) while bash parses `'-v'` as the option. The subscript is single-quoted so the reader never reads the substitution it carries; on a bash that evaluates a printf -v subscript (the case bx13 was written for) that starts a real tool by a relative path. I did not run it on a bash 5; this finding rests on the reader accepting it, and on the executor's own reason for refusing `printf -v`. bx13 proves only the unquoted spelling.
findings.resolution: Require the format's decoded text, not its quoting, to be safe: accept printf only when args[0] is single-quoted AND its text does not start with `'-` (or require it to contain a `%` conversion and no leading dash), and add a bp10 row `printf '-v' x y` and a bx13 twin with the option quoted.
